title: I don’t like the new update
text:
The app was pretty good before and was relatively customizable but with this new update you’re literally not allowed to delete certain categories. I don’t track my emergency fund through this app but when it updated it had added the emergency fund line back plus put an amount in. When I try to delete it so my budget isn’t crowded with lines I don’t use, I get a pop up telling me I can’t delete it because emergency savings is important and I should be doing it. It feels like I’m getting lectured by an app.

You’re not even allowed to change the name of the emergency fund and use it for something else. It just has to sit there, empty and cluttering up the budget lines. 

I pay $17.99 monthly for this app. I should be able to customize it as much as I like. 

What was really needed instead in this update was the ability to put biweekly paychecks on a consistent schedule so you don’t need to go in on the first of every month and change the date on each paycheck and then go literally line by line and change the income date for each budget line. I wish you could just select “Biweekly pay schedule” and put in the first dates and then it calculates that your next pay will be in two more weeks.


Edit: For the love of god, please stop changing the layout of the app and making it less and less customizable.

title: Live Long Enough to Become the Villain
text:
I have been a loyal, paying annual subscriber of EveryDollar since 2020. I would let everyone know how Financial Peace University and this app specifically helped our family stay on track for budgeting. I’ve even paid for multiple people who saw the annual fee too high of an entry fee.
Life gets really busy sometimes, and even though both me and my wife are on the same page about our budget I’m the one who keeps track (the nerd). And sometimes I fall behind, but that’s ok because I know where I left off and I know where we’re at. I’m able to go back and make all my changes to our budget.
But a recent unannounced update has severely degraded the app’s usability for how we budget.
EveryDollar recently rolled out a forced "Month Close" feature that automatically locks budgets that are more than two months old. There was absolutely no advance warning, email notice, or in-app countdown before this went live. If you are someone who reconciles transactions or adjusts budgets every few weeks or months, you will suddenly find yourself completely locked out of editing your OWN historical data.
When you pay for a full year upfront, you expect feature stability. Forcing a massive structural change that alters how users interact with their financial data—without an option to toggle it off—is incredibly disappointing. 
I have reached out to support multiple times regarding this issue to no avail.
If you need flexibility in your budgeting tool and want control over your past data, I highly recommend looking elsewhere before locking yourself into a yearly subscription here.
If EveryDollar changes this to be an optional feature my review will absolutely amend this review and will renew my annual subscription.

title: Please Allow Users to Reopen and Edit Previous Budgets
text:
I’ve used EveryDollar for years, and the new policy preventing edits to budgets older than two months creates a serious problem for users who need to reconcile past transactions.

I hadn’t finished assigning all my September income and expenses before November started, and now I can’t complete that budget. Because I use multiple bank accounts, credit cards, and sinking funds, this also affects my ability to accurately track fund balances and carry money forward into October.

I understand the need to protect rollover calculations, but permanently locking previous months shouldn’t be the solution. Please add an option to reopen closed budgets and automatically recalculate affected balances in subsequent months. Even a warning explaining that editing a previous month will affect future budgets would be reasonable.

At the very least, users should have a way to request an unlock, complete their reconciliation, and update their fund balances without manually rebuilding everything in another month.

Budgeting doesn’t always happen on a perfect schedule, and users need the flexibility to correct their financial records. I genuinely want to continue using EveryDollar, but this restriction makes accurate budgeting unnecessarily difficult. Please reconsider this policy and provide a practical way to edit and reconcile older months.

I’ve been complaining about the badge being wrong all the time for the last several updates—for perhaps a year. I can tell you’ve done something but it’s still consistently wrong, just wrong in a different way. Aggravating.

The app is mostly good. But the app badge is really screwed up. It shows that there are transactions to log when there are none or else the number is wrong. If there are any, after I log them, a couple minutes later the badge shows that there 3 new transactions, but there are always none. It does this consistently.

If it shows a number of transactions to log at other times (not the 3 it shows right after I’ve logged all transactions), the number of actual transactions is always one fewer than what the badge indicates.

The badge is almost always wrong now. Completely unreliable.

Irritating. I pay a LOT of money for this service, so please fix.

title: Funds and Savings
text: Everything works fine but I wish there was a way to transfer money within the app instead of having to make two transactions to show that you moved money from one account to another. Also there should be a way to make savings goals that can be updated as you put the money in and can also be carried over to the next month.

title: The Dollar App
text: Seems like a great application.     7 day trial was great. My only concern is $80.00 bucks year.  To me, should be free in helping folks get out of debt.  Not just 7 days.

title: I’m looking for another budget app
text: How can you possibly keep making this app worse with every update. I’ve had this for at least six years and it consistently keeps getting worse. Who in the heck is in charge? Why do we have to jump through all these hoops to move stuff around and push five different buttons just to put an expense in. And why the heck can I not use the same wording in a different month. Is that really that big of a deal?!

title: Too much tinkering
text: Ive used this app for about 7 years. Imo it was fine and a great app about 5 years ago and then they started regularly making changes to it. Its not that complicated of a concept but someone is always messing around and trying to change the way something looks or functions. This latest update with the calculator on the keyboard is just really stupid. Why would you need a calculator when you are recording transactions?! It makes it too tricky to use for older folks like me who can barely type on these phones. Im going to just make a spreadsheet and use that if the developers keep getting creative. Please guys, just keep it simple. Know a good thing when you have it and let it be. Otherwise, very useful. I credit this app above all else with me having a firm grip on my money.

title: Would be great but…
text: Simple and easy to use. It doesn’t require you to link your bank accounts which is exactly what I wanted- I prefer to manually enter my transactions. Unfortunately it keeps logging me out and losing months of budgets when I log back in making it unusable. Logging back in is annoying enough on its own but each time it deletes 10+ months of budgets and transactions including the current month. It does this maybe every 1.5 to 2 months so I gave it a couple more chances in case it was a glitch that just happened once or twice but nope. It happened again. Deleted all of my budgets and transactions from December 2025 to current day (Sept 2026). And it’s almost the end of the month so I’m not going to go back in and redo weeks of transactions just for this to happen again in a month or two.

title: New Calculator Not User Friendly
text: Have used the app for a long time and pay for premium. This new calculator update may cause me to unsubscribe. You can’t hold the back button and erase a full number. The typing is slow and requires a done press. Developers should revert back to the one before.

title: Cash Flow feature now costs money to use after latest update!
text: With the latest update, the Cash Flow feature now costs money to use! It’s literally the main thing I use this app for, super frustrating as I’ve been using this app for the last year and it’s been great! Bad move, Ramsey!

title: So hard to use
text: Wish I could do 0 stars do NOT use this app if you want to budget

title: Calculator Keys
text: Please get rid of the calculator keys - who asked for that??? All I want to do is manually enter my transaction amount. Having to work around a calculator buttons on half my screen with no way to turn off is frustrating. So many unnecessary changes make the app worse, not better.

title: Pod
text: This app is lame they make you pay for a year automatically if you download it for free and don’t Intend on paying for it. I don’t recommend using it. Now I have on call Apple instead of the people so I can get my money back what a pain

title: Better on computer
text: The computer/online version is great. The mobile app sucks at syncing data across different devices. Many times i have had to re-reconcile various transactions because of a failure to sync correctly from the mobile app. Watch out for duplicate transactions!

title: Works well until it doesn’t!
text: Im glad I downloaded the free version, its great, but it crashed after four weeks and I can’t login anymore. It has been three days so far, I found another expense tracker. Again, its great if it works! Again, it’s the best app, if it’s working! Maybe stick to the free version until you can trust it enough! Nevertheless, I’ve deleted and downloaded the app multiple times. I you must be online to login expenses.
